messages:
Priya Nair: hey team :wave: quick sync — we need a compact POC "runbook" for the AcmeBank pilot. scope: prompt inventory + baseline prompts, eval rubric, acceptance criteria, timeline (3 weeks). can we align owners and what's minimal to ship a credible demo?

Alex Carter: +1. can we treat this like two tracks: (1) prompt & eval engineering, (2) infra/pricing/security checklist. i can take infra/pricing.

Jordan Lee: i can own prompt inventory + baseline prompts. i'll start a sheet. do we have a canonical prompt template?

Priya Nair: Jordan — thanks. template for each prompt row: use_case, user_intent, prompt_text, example_inputs, expected_output_format, success_metric, eval_set_size, owner. put a short example row first.

Jordan Lee: adding sample rows now. short example:
```
use_case: customer support reply suggestion
user_intent: summarize recent conversation and propose next steps
prompt_text: "Given the conversation below, summarize the key points and suggest 2 concise next-step responses for the agent."
example_inputs: "Cust: ... Agent: ..."
expected_output_format: JSON {"summary":"...","options":["...","..."]}
success_metric: 80% helpfulness on eval set (human-rated), avg tokens <= 120
eval_set_size: 30
owner: Jordan Lee
```

Kai Müller: as a note on evals: prefer small focused evals per use case (20-50 examples) so we can iterate fast. add both automated pass/fail (regex/JSON schema) and subjective human rating.

Alex Carter: infra/pricing notes: for the demo we should scope capacity to ~50 concurrent short chats — estimate ~0.5 vGPU-hours/day if using batching and prefix cache. rough cost delta: hosted = $X per 100k tokens, dedicated reserved = negotiated. i'll confirm numbers with pricing team tomorrow.

Priya Nair: security & data flow — we need a short blurb for the SOC questionnaire (no PHI, PD, PII persist). @Kai do we have the SaaS dataflow diagram we can link?

Kai Müller: yes — iteration A is in our docs: https://redwood.example/docs/saas-dataflow — i'll paste sanitized snippet into the runbook. also note: customer requires KMS-backed key management for Private; mark as blocker for Private option.

Jordan Lee: quick question on baseline prompts: do we want quantized model variants in the baseline? e.g., 8-bit for cost path, float16 for quality path.

Priya Nair: include both. baseline = 1) quality (float16, tuned prompt) and 2) cost path (quantized, tuned short prompt). acceptance criteria should be model-variant specific. example: quality path >= 85% human helpfulness, cost path >= 75% with 30% token reduction.

Alex Carter: for the sales demo, also include fallback policy: if latency > 1s for >10% of requests, route to cheaper compatible model and flag in dashboard. that avoids blowing SLA during load spikes.

OpsBot: eval-run finished: 1975006840 — 30/30 automated schema checks passed for customer-support prompts (run id r-8421). link: https://redwood.example/evals/r-8421

Jordan Lee: nice. i'll extract the failing/human-review items from the run and add to the sheet.

Priya Nair: next steps: Jordan — share sheet link by EOD, include 2 exemplar prompts per use case + 30 evals for top 2 use cases. Alex — confirm cost numbers and fallback routing config tomorrow. Kai — add sanitized dataflow img + security note on KMS. i'll collate an executive summary and success criteria doc for the AE.

Alex Carter: got it. FYI i've added a short note on licensing questions: customer asked about model licensing for 3rd-party open models — we'll need legal to confirm redistribution rights if we bundle model binaries in Private.

Priya Nair: thanks. can everyone react with :thumbsup: when you've added your bits so I know it's ready for the AE handoff?

Alex Carter: :thumbsup: (Alex)

Jordan Lee: :thumbsup: (Jordan)

Kai Müller: :thumbsup: (Kai)

Priya Nair: perfect — closing loop. i'll post the handoff note to the AE channel once the sheet is updated.
